In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

suppression of inflammation is important in the infarction heart and that there is a need for further research into the molecular mechanisms of suppression and containment of inflammation in the postinfarcted heart.
the inflammatory response in myocardial repair is a complex, tightly regulated process, and that its dysregulation may be an important determinant of adverse remodeling and heart failure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to better understand the mechanisms of inflammation resolution in order to develop better therapeutic strategies to treat heart failure.
the inflammatory response to cardiac necrosis is a tightly controlled process that is regulated by endogenous signals that restrain and terminate the inflammatory cascade.

the inflammatory response is a critical component in the process of myocardial repair and that the balance between proinflammatory and prorepair mediators determines the extent of cardiac remodeling and functional outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resolution of inflammation is a critical process in the infarction heart, and that the lack of this process may lead to adverse outcomes.

the resolution of inflammation is an active process, and that the postinfarct inflammatory response is tightly regulated by a number of endogenous signals that limit extension of the inflammatory cascade and prevent adverse remodeling.
suppression and resolution of inflammation may play an active and beneficial role in cardiac repair and that targeting these processes may be beneficial for patients with myocardial ischemia.
